conventions.convention: A laboratory region is a restricted inertial chart with nonempty open spatial Ω and nonempty open time interval I, x⁰=ct, signature (−,+,+,+), and positively oriented Euclidean spatial basis. Fields are maps Ω×I→Rᵐ; fixed-time readings are spatial maps. A frame, chart, point observer, congruence and tetrad are distinct objects.

SI is used: c and e have exact defining values; μ₀ is experimentally determined; ε₀=(μ₀c²)⁻¹. The quoted relative uncertainty 2.3×10⁻¹⁰ concerns the historical 2019 adoption estimate, not a current measurement. This distinction agrees with the independently opened [BIPM SI brochure](https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/41483022/SI-Brochure-9.pdf), §2.3.1.

Charge q is a real model parameter. Frame densities are ρ and J; the adopted four-current is j=(cρ,J). For a general factorization j=ρ₀U, ρ=ρ₀U⁰/c. The convective identities ρ=γρ₀ and J=ρv require the additional normalization η(U,U)=−c².
E is polar and B axial under spatial orthogonal coordinate changes. Classical fields have explicitly stated joint regularity; singular-support values are not supplied by their definition.

The electromagnetic tensor uses F₀ᵢ=−Eᵢ/c and Fᵢⱼ=εᵢⱼₖBₖ, hence Fⁱ⁰=−Eᵢ/c. With ε₀₁₂₃=+1, observer components are eᵢ=Eᵢ/c and bᵢ=−Bᵢ. The optional SI tensor in the SR supplier is the negative of this entire tensor.

The original Maxwell postulate has a jointly C¹ classical branch and a locally integrable field/source weak branch. Nonzero point and sheet distributions require the separate singular-source adoption; defining a weak solution predicate does not adopt a physical law.

Volume tests have compact closure inside Ω, specified finite piecewise C¹ boundary presentations and outward normals. Patch tests are regular C² parametrizations over finite elementary Green regions, with induced boundary orientation and positive Stokes sign. Tests are stationary; differential recovery requires every admissible test, not one selected geometry.

Distribution pairings are bilinear without conjugation; derivatives move onto tests with a minus sign. Point histories require properness for zero endpoint residuals. Sheets are compact, stationary, without edges, and carry tangential K. General weak fields need no traces; jump conclusions require their separate trace hypotheses. Countable Choice is carried where the measure interfaces require it.

For stationary interfaces n points from Ω₋ to Ω₊ and [F]=F₊−F₋. Joint one-sided C¹ extensions yield all-time pointwise jumps. The weaker branch requires locally integrable piecewise derivatives and sheet traces and initially yields almost-everywhere conclusions; joint continuity supplies the all-time upgrade.

Pure electrostatics is time independence together with B=J=0 in one named frame. Its smooth spatial equations are div E=ρ/ε₀ and curl E=0. Staticity is not asserted to survive a boost or to imply mechanical equilibrium.

The three-dimensional Newtonian kernel is Φ(x)=1/(4π|x|), with −ΔTΦ=δ₀; electrostatic potential is φ=ε₀⁻¹Nρ and E=−∇φ. Decaying uniqueness is for compact C¹ volume sources and C² potentials, not an asserted point-source uniqueness theorem.

The Lorentz test-particle law uses constant q, supplied m>0, a future timelike C² worldline and prescribed C¹ external field, excluding its self-field. Continuum force and power densities require an explicitly applicable matter model. Field energy is not identified with particle rest mass.

load_bearing.statement: On the declared laboratory region, with μ₀,c>0 and ε₀=(μ₀c²)⁻¹, adopt div E=ρ/ε₀, div B=0, curl E=−∂tB and curl B=μ₀J+c⁻²∂tE: pointwise for the stated jointly C¹ fields and continuous sources, or distributionally for locally integrable fields and sources. Point and sheet sources lacking locally integrable representatives are excluded.

Defines locally integrable weak fields, point-source pairings with proper-history or finite-endpoint qualifications, compact stationary-sheet pairings with continuous σ and tangential continuous K, and the four vanishing Maxwell residual pairings for volume-plus-declared-singular sources. Classical trace branches are optional additional hypotheses; no products of distributions, existence theorem or physical adoption follows from the predicate.

Under Countable Choice, adopt the four distributional Maxwell identities for the locally integrable fields and volume-plus-point or compact stationary-sheet sources of def-em-weak-sources. Only tuples satisfying the identities are models; existence for every prescribed source is not asserted.

Jointly C² fields and C¹ sources satisfying the smooth Maxwell branch obey ∂tρ+div J=0 pointwise. Arbitrary field and source distributions satisfying the four displayed Maxwell identities obey the same continuity identity distributionally. This is a compatibility implication, without physical adoption of arbitrary distributions.

Under Countable Choice and the stated joint regularity, the four smooth Maxwell equations imply the two volume-flux and two patch-circulation identities for every test geometry of def-em-fixed-test-geometry and every t∈I, including differentiability of the fixed-patch fluxes. Conversely, those identities and flux differentiability for every such geometry and time imply all four pointwise equations.

Under Countable Choice, a fixed compact embedded C² two-sided interface, continuous σ and tangential K, the stated jointly one-sided C¹ fields and locally integrable volume sources, and the adopted weak Maxwell identities give n·[E]=σ/ε₀, n×[B]=μ₀K, n·[B]=0 and n×[E]=0 pointwise on S×I. With separate spatial C¹ traces plus the stated local integrability hypotheses, the sheet pairings vanish and the identities hold for every spatial point for almost every time; joint continuity upgrades them to every time.

Jointly C² fields and C¹ sources satisfying the two Maxwell evolution equations and, independently, source continuity have ∂tD_B=∂tD_E=0; their Gauss defects are constant on I. The derivative conclusion also holds for arbitrary distributions satisfying those identities. Under Countable Choice, continuous representatives of distributional defects are time independent. Evolution plus continuity and zero defects at one time recover all four Maxwell identities in the stated smooth or continuous-representative branch.

Under Countable Choice, for real compactly supported C¹ ρ on R³, φ=ε₀⁻¹Nρ is C², E=−∇φ satisfies the electrostatic equations and the everywhere absolutely convergent Coulomb integral, with the stated far-field bounds; φ is the unique C² Poisson solution vanishing at infinity. For compact L¹ ρ, Nρ is finite almost everywhere, locally integrable, smooth harmonic off the support, and solves Poisson distributionally. For q∈R and x₀∈R³, the displayed ideal point potential and field are locally integrable, smooth off x₀, and satisfy −ΔTφq=div Eq=(q/ε₀)δx₀ and curl Eq=0 distributionally; no point-source uniqueness or self-force is asserted.

For a nonempty open Ω⊂R³ star-shaped about a∈Ω, C¹ E and continuous ρ satisfying div E=ρ/ε₀ and curl E=0, φ(x)=−∫₀¹E(a+s(x−a))·(x−a)ds is C² with ∇φ=−E and −Δφ=ρ/ε₀. Every other C² potential with that gradient differs by one constant on Ω; no boundary or infinity normalization is supplied.

Under Countable Choice, for real ρ∈C¹_c(R³) and its smooth Coulomb potential and field, the finite quantities (ε₀/2)∫|E|², (1/2)∫ρφ and (1/(2ε₀))∬Φ(x−y)ρ(x)ρ(y) are equal. The assembly reading uses the ideal quasistatic bookkeeping family ρs=sρ with external support, without a time-dependent matter model or rest-mass identification.

Under Countable Choice, for n≥2, p∈Rⁿ and u∈L¹_loc(Rⁿ) that is C¹ off p with every classical partial, extended by zero at p, locally integrable, ∂iTu=T∂iu for every coordinate i. The exceptional set is one point, not a hypersurface.

Under Countable Choice, for n≥3 and real f∈L¹(Rⁿ) vanishing almost everywhere outside a closed ball of radius R>0, Nf is C¹ on |x|>2R, ∇Nf(x)=∫∇Φ(x−y)f(y)dy absolutely, and |∇Nf(x)|≤2ⁿ⁻¹‖f‖₁/(ωn−1|x|ⁿ⁻¹). Nothing is asserted in |x|≤2R.

seams_checked.note: Concrete signature and contraction operator are preserved. The postulate explicitly distinguishes the supplier's future causal cone from the SR future timelike C⁺ convention.

The two-form definition uses the general observer decomposition and converts the optional SI dictionary by negating the entire tensor. The C¹-potential closedness calculation uses the stated compact-variation integration-by-parts and localization clauses.
The point-source example retains the proper-graph condition and consumes the distributional continuity conclusion; it does not infer a singular-source Maxwell adoption.

Point endpoint signs, compact stationary-interface assumptions and n·[F]/n×[F] surface terms are preserved. Fixed parameter-integral hypotheses are checked on compact neighborhoods; the jump theorem supplies its additional spacetime qualifications locally.

Potential uses retain star-shapedness and interior C² regularity without claiming boundary regularity. Image calculations consume the point-charge distributional identities. Capacitance assembly is derived directly and explicitly avoids applying the smooth volume-source energy theorem to sheets.

Exterior multipoles consume the compact L¹ potential branch with its almost-everywhere finiteness and distributional Poisson identity; classical field conclusions require the additional C¹ compact-source branch.

Steady-current continuity uses the distributional compatibility theorem and states when the conclusion is pointwise. Line and noncompact-sheet models are explicitly outside the earlier weak-source classes and receive a separate adoption.

Material sheet pairings retain stationary compact support and tangential current conventions. Distributional macroscopic interface equations are an explicit additional hypothesis, not a consequence claimed from the smooth rewriting theorem.

The cited source-free equations are identified as two equations of the smooth Maxwell branch. Potential and gauge items retain their own domain and regularity conditions; sourced equivalences use the four equations with the same SI constants.

Balance items state jointly C¹ fields, continuous sources and the exact Maxwell equations. Force and power readings require the applicable continuum matter model; total conservation additionally assumes matter balances and retains boundary flux.

The IVP cites Gauss propagation with the evolution equations and independently required continuity. Source-free wave implications preserve joint C² regularity; interference invokes only finite same-branch superposition with real coefficients.
